notes.gomesi: The long traditional dress worn by women, also called busuuti.
notes.kkanzu: The long white robe worn by men on formal days.
notes.yange: For one n- thing: essaati yange, my shirt.
notes.zange: For many n- things: engatto zange, my shoes.
notes.eno: For one n- thing: essaati eno, this shirt.
notes.ngitwala: For n- things. Compare nkitwala for eki- things.

guidebook.intro: Clothes words bring in the n- class, one of the largest noun classes. Its nouns usually start with **en-**, **em-** or a doubled consonant like **essaati**.

tips.title: “My” with n- nouns
body: One n- thing takes **yange**: **essaati yange**, **empale yange**. Many n- things take **zange**: **engatto zange**, **engoye zange**.
Many n- nouns look the same in the singular and the plural. **Engatto** is one shoe or several; **zange** or **yange** tells you which.

tips.title: “This” agrees too
body: You learnt **kino** (this) for eki- things in Unit 4. For an n- thing it is **eno**: **essaati eno** (this shirt). And “I’ll take it” changes its middle: **nkitwala** for an eki- thing, **ngitwala** for an n- thing.

culture.title: Gomesi and kanzu
body: The **gomesi** (or **busuuti**) is a long, brightly coloured dress with puffed shoulders and a sash, worn by women at weddings, introductions and church. The **kkanzu** is a long white robe for men, often with a jacket over it.
Wearing them to a ceremony is a sign of respect, and visitors who do are warmly welcomed.

culture.title: Shoes off
body: In many homes, guests take off their shoes at the door. If you see shoes lined up outside, **yambula engatto**.
